# Page: Project Structure

# Project Structure

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.gitmodules](.gitmodules)
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [docs/docs_requirements.txt](docs/docs_requirements.txt)
- [docs/source/_static/ga.js](docs/source/_static/ga.js)
- [docs/source/conf.py](docs/source/conf.py)
- [docs/source/contributing_link.rst](docs/source/contributing_link.rst)
- [docs/source/index.rst](docs/source/index.rst)
- [models/rf3/configs/experiment/pretrained/rf3.yaml](models/rf3/configs/experiment/pretrained/rf3.yaml)
- [models/rf3/src/rf3/callbacks/dump_validation_structures.py](models/rf3/src/rf3/callbacks/dump_validation_structures.py)
- [models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py](models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py)
- [models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py](models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py)
- [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/cli.py](models/rfd3/src/rfd3/cli.py)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)

</details>



This page documents the organization of the Foundry repository, including the directory layout, package dependencies, and relationships between components. For information about setting up a development environment, see [Development Setup](#11.2). For details about specific model implementations, refer to [RFdiffusion3 (RFD3)](#4), [RosettaFold3 (RF3)](#5), and [ProteinMPNN and LigandMPNN](#6).

## Repository Organization

Foundry is organized as a multi-package repository with a strict dependency hierarchy. The core `rc-foundry` package provides shared training infrastructure and utilities, while individual model packages (`rfd3`, `rf3`, `mpnn`, `rfd3na`) are independently installable and depend on both `foundry` and `atomworks` [CONTRIBUTING.md:12-18]().

### Top-Level Directory Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    root["foundry/ (repository root)"]
    
    root --> src_foundry["src/foundry/<br/>Core infrastructure"]
    root --> src_cli["src/foundry_cli/<br/>Checkpoint CLI"]
    root --> models["models/<br/>Model packages"]
    root --> docs["docs/<br/>Documentation"]
    
    models --> rfd3["models/rfd3/<br/>RFdiffusion3"]
    models --> rf3["models/rf3/<br/>RosettaFold3"]
    models --> mpnn["models/mpnn/<br/>ProteinMPNN/LigandMPNN"]
    models --> rfd3na["models/rfd3na/<br/>RFdiffusion3NA"]
    
    rfd3 --> rfd3_src["src/rfd3/"]
    rfd3 --> rfd3_configs["configs/"]
    
    rf3 --> rf3_src["src/rf3/"]
    rf3 --> rf3_configs["configs/"]
    
    mpnn --> mpnn_src["src/mpnn/"]
    
    src_foundry --> foundry_utils["utils/"]
    src_foundry --> foundry_callbacks["callbacks/"]
```

**Sources:** [pyproject.toml:117-124](), [CONTRIBUTING.md:12-18]()

### Package Dependency Flow

The repository enforces a strict dependency hierarchy to maintain clean separation of concerns:

```mermaid
graph TD
    user["End User / Researcher"]
    
    subgraph "Foundry Packages"
        rfd3["models.rfd3<br/>RFdiffusion3"]
        rf3["models.rf3<br/>RosettaFold3"]
        mpnn["models.mpnn<br/>ProteinMPNN"]
        rfd3na["models.rfd3na<br/>RFdiffusion3NA"]
        
        foundry["foundry<br/>FabricTrainer<br/>BaseCallback"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Dependencies"
        atomworks["atomworks<br/>AtomArray<br/>Structure I/O"]
    end
    
    user --> rfd3
    user --> rf3
    user --> mpnn
    user --> rfd3na
    
    rfd3 --> foundry
    rf3 --> foundry
    mpnn --> foundry
    rfd3na --> foundry
    
    foundry --> atomworks
    rfd3 --> atomworks
    rf3 --> atomworks
```

**Key principle:** `foundry` → `atomworks` (one-way dependency). All models within Foundry use AtomWorks for manipulating and processing biomolecular structures in both training and inference [CONTRIBUTING.md:12-18]().

**Sources:** [CONTRIBUTING.md:12-18](), [pyproject.toml:47-51]()

## Core Package Structure

The `foundry` package provides shared infrastructure used by all models:

**Diagram: Foundry Core Module Organization**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "src/foundry/"
        callbacks["callbacks/<br/>callback.py"]
        utils_dir["utils/<br/>ddp.py<br/>logging.py<br/>alignment.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "src/foundry_cli/"
        cli_pkg["download_checkpoints.py<br/>Entry point for 'foundry' CLI"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Key Classes and Functions"
        callbacks --> base_callback["callback.py:<br/>BaseCallback"]
        
        utils_dir --> ddp_utils["ddp.py:<br/>RankedLogger"]
        
        utils_dir --> logging_utils["logging.py:<br/>RankedLogger<br/>suppress_warnings()"]
        
        utils_dir --> alignment_utils["alignment.py:<br/>weighted_rigid_align()"]
    end
```

**Core modules:**

| Module | Key Classes/Functions | Purpose |
|--------|----------------------|---------|
| `foundry.callbacks` | `BaseCallback` | Base class for training/inference hooks [models/rf3/src/rf3/callbacks/dump_validation_structures.py:12-15]() |
| `foundry.utils.logging` | `RankedLogger`, `suppress_warnings()` | Centralized logging and warning management [models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py:21-23]() |
| `foundry.utils.alignment` | `weighted_rigid_align()` | Rigid body alignment for trajectories [models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py:12-12]() |
| `foundry_cli` | `download_checkpoints:app` | Checkpoint management CLI [pyproject.toml:94-94]() |

**Sources:** [pyproject.toml:89-94](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/callbacks/dump_validation_structures.py:12-15](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py:12-12]()

## Model Package Structure

Each model package under `models/` is treated as an independent package with its own `src/` and `configs/` [CONTRIBUTING.md:61-70]().

### Model-Specific Entry Points

Each model provides its own CLI entry point through `pyproject.toml`:

**Diagram: CLI Entry Points and Implementation**

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "pyproject.toml [project.scripts]"
        scripts["[project.scripts]"]
        
        scripts --> rfd3_ep["rfd3 = rfd3.cli:app"]
        scripts --> rf3_ep["rf3 = rf3.cli:app"]
        scripts --> mpnn_ep["mpnn = mpnn.inference:main"]
        scripts --> rfd3na_ep["rfd3na = rfd3na.cli:app"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CLI Implementation Files"
        rfd3_cli["models/rfd3/src/rfd3/cli.py"]
        rf3_cli["models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py"]
        mpnn_inf["models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CLI Commands"
        rfd3_ep --> rfd3_cli
        rfd3_cli --> rfd3_design["@app.command() design()"]
        
        rf3_ep --> rf3_cli
        rf3_cli --> rf3_fold["@app.command() fold()"]
        rf3_cli --> rf3_predict["@app.command() predict()"]
    end
```

| Model | Command | Entry Point | Implementation |
|-------|---------|-------------|----------------|
| RFD3 | `rfd3 design` | `rfd3.cli:app` | [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/cli.py:9-12]() |
| RF3 | `rf3 fold` / `rf3 predict` | `rf3.cli:app` | [models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py:9-83]() |
| MPNN | `mpnn` | `mpnn.inference:main` | [pyproject.toml:93-93]() |
| RFD3NA | `rfd3na` | `rfd3na.cli:app` | [pyproject.toml:92-92]() |

**Sources:** [pyproject.toml:89-94](), [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/cli.py:1-48](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py:1-87]()

## Configuration System

Foundry uses Hydra for configuration. Model CLIs locate their configs by checking for development vs. installed modes [models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py:25-39]().

**Diagram: Hydra Configuration Resolution**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "CLI Logic (e.g., RF3)"
        rf3_cli["rf3/cli.py"]
        rf3_cli --> check_mode["Check if 'configs/' is sibling<br/>(Installed vs Dev)"]
        check_mode --> init_hydra["initialize_config_dir(config_path)"]
        init_hydra --> compose_cfg["compose(config_name='inference', overrides=args)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Config Structure"
        rfd3_configs["models/rfd3/configs/"]
        rfd3_configs --> rfd3_inf["inference.yaml"]
        
        rf3_configs["models/rf3/configs/"]
        rf3_configs --> rf3_inf["inference.yaml"]
        rf3_configs --> rf3_exp["experiment/pretrained/rf3.yaml"]
    end
```

**Key configuration handling:**
- **Dynamic Config Paths:** CLIs like `rf3` and `rfd3` automatically detect if they are running from a source checkout or an installed site-package to find the correct `configs/` directory [models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py:28-39](), [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/cli.py:18-24]().
- **Default Engines:** CLIs ensure a default `inference_engine` is set if not provided in overrides (e.g., `inference_engine=rf3`) [models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py:53-59](), [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/cli.py:30-34]().

**Sources:** [models/rf3/src/rf3/cli.py:25-69](), [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/cli.py:14-43]()

### Build and Packaging

The repository uses `hatchling` as the build backend and explicitly includes model source and config directories in the wheel [pyproject.toml:102-124]().

```toml
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = [
  "src/foundry",
  "src/foundry_cli",
  "models/rf3/src/rf3",
  "models/rfd3/src/rfd3",
  # ...
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"models/rfd3na/configs" = "rfd3na/configs"
"models/rfd3/configs" = "rfd3/configs"
"models/rf3/configs" = "rf3/configs"
```

**Sources:** [pyproject.toml:116-130]()

## Data Flow and I/O Utilities

Models share I/O patterns for structure generation and validation.

**Diagram: Structure Output Flow**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Validation/Inference Output"
        callback["DumpValidationStructuresCallback"]
        io_utils["rf3.utils.io"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AtomWorks Integration"
        atom_array["biotite.AtomArray"]
        to_cif["atomworks.io.utils.io_utils:to_cif_file"]
    end
    
    callback --> build_stack["build_stack_from_atom_array_and_batched_coords"]
    build_stack --> dump_struct["dump_structures"]
    dump_struct --> to_cif
```

**Key I/O Functions:**
- `build_stack_from_atom_array_and_batched_coords`: Converts raw coordinates into a `biotite.AtomArrayStack` and handles `chain_id` adjustments for multiple transformations [models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py:61-94]().
- `dump_structures`: High-level wrapper to save structures to CIF/PDB, supporting single or multi-model files [models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py:97-138]().
- `dump_trajectories`: Handles denoising trajectories, including rigid alignment to the final prediction [models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py:141-174]().

**Sources:** [models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py:61-174](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/callbacks/dump_validation_structures.py:15-101]()

## Contributing a New Model

To add a new model to the Foundry ecosystem:
1. Create `models/<model_name>/` with a `pyproject.toml` [CONTRIBUTING.md:67-67]().
2. Add `rc-foundry` as a dependency [CONTRIBUTING.md:68-68]().
3. Implement logic in `models/<model_name>/src/` [CONTRIBUTING.md:69-69]().
4. Add the package to the root `pyproject.toml` wheel targets for distribution [pyproject.toml:116-124]().

**Sources:** [CONTRIBUTING.md:61-70](), [pyproject.toml:116-124]()

# Development Setup

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/lint_production.yaml](.github/workflows/lint_production.yaml)

- [docs/docs_requirements.txt](docs/docs_requirements.txt)
- [docs/source/_static/ga.js](docs/source/_static/ga.js)
- [docs/source/conf.py](docs/source/conf.py)
- [docs/source/contributing_link.rst](docs/source/contributing_link.rst)
- [docs/source/index.rst](docs/source/index.rst)
- [models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py](models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py)
- [models/rf3/src/rf3/validate.py](models/rf3/src/rf3/validate.py)
- [models/rf3/tests/conftest.py](models/rf3/tests/conftest.py)

</details>



This page provides instructions for setting up a development environment to contribute to or extend the Foundry codebase. For basic installation and usage, see [Installation](#2.1). For project structure details, see [Project Structure](#11.1). For contribution guidelines, see [Contributing](#11.3).

## Prerequisites

**Python Version**: Foundry requires Python 3.12 or higher.

**Package Manager**: Development uses `uv`, a fast Python package installer and resolver. Install it first:

```bash
pip install uv
```

**Git Repository**: Clone the Foundry repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RosettaCommons/foundry.git
cd foundry
```

**Sources**: [.github/workflows/lint_production.yaml:26-27](), [CONTRIBUTING.md:20-24]()

## Installation for Development

### Editable Installation

Install the entire Foundry ecosystem in editable mode for development. This allows you to modify shared utilities and see changes immediately across all models.

```bash
uv pip install -e '.[all,dev]'
```

This command installs:
- Core `foundry` package from `src/foundry/`
- All model packages located in `models/`
- All optional dependencies (`[all]`)
- Development tools (`[dev]`) including `ruff` and `pre-commit`

**Sources**: [CONTRIBUTING.md:20-29](), [CONTRIBUTING.md:62-65]()

### Development Dependencies

The `[dev]` extra includes tools for linting, formatting, and building documentation.

| Category | Tools |
|----------|-------|
| Linting & Formatting | `ruff`, `pre-commit` |
| Documentation | `sphinx`, `myst-parser`, `furo`, `sphinx-copybutton` |
| Build System | `Makefile` |

**Sources**: [docs/docs_requirements.txt:1-4](), [.github/workflows/lint_production.yaml:28-33](), [CONTRIBUTING.md:43-49]()

## Development Environment Structure

The following diagram illustrates the development environment setup and how the configuration flows from the environment and repository root to the specific model implementations.

**Foundry Development Architecture**
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Repository Root"
        RootConfig["pyproject.toml<br/>Global settings"]
        SrcFoundry["src/foundry/<br/>Core shared logic"]
        ModelsDir["models/<br/>Sub-packages"]
        EnvFile[".env<br/>Local paths"]
        Makefile["Makefile<br/>Dev commands"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Packages"
        RFD3["models/rfd3/<br/>pyproject.toml<br/>configs/"]
        RF3["models/rf3/<br/>pyproject.toml<br/>configs/"]
        MPNN["models/mpnn/<br/>pyproject.toml"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dev Tools"
        Ruff["ruff<br/>Lint/Format"]
        PreCommit[".pre-commit-config.yaml"]
        Sphinx["docs/<br/>Sphinx builder"]
    end
    
    RootConfig --> RFD3
    RootConfig --> RF3
    RootConfig --> MPNN
    
    EnvFile -.->|loaded by| RF3Train["models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py"]
    EnvFile -.->|loaded by| RF3Val["models/rf3/src/rf3/validate.py"]
    
    Makefile --> Ruff
    PreCommit --> Makefile
    
    SrcFoundry --> RFD3
    SrcFoundry --> RF3
```

**Sources**: [CONTRIBUTING.md:12-19](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py:18](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/validate.py:13](), [Makefile:16-18]()

## Environment Configuration

### Creating the .env File

Foundry relies on a `.env` file to manage local paths for data mirrors and external tools. This file is loaded at runtime by scripts using `dotenv`.

```python
# In training/inference scripts
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv(override=True)
```

**Sources**: [models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py:18](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/validate.py:13]()

### Required Path Management

Training and validation scripts resolve project roots and configuration paths dynamically to ensure they work across different environments.

| Script | Root Resolution | Config Path |
|----------|---------|---------------|
| `train.py` | `rootutils.setup_root` | `models/rf3/configs` |
| `validate.py` | `rootutils.setup_root` | `models/rf3/configs` |

**Sources**: [models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py:16-20](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/validate.py:17-19]()

## Development Tools Setup

### Pre-commit Hooks and Formatting

Foundry uses `ruff` for both linting and formatting. A `Makefile` is provided to simplify these operations.

**Enable Git Hooks**:
```bash
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

**Manual Formatting**:
To format the `src`, `models`, and `tests` directories, run:
```bash
make format
```
This executes `ruff format` followed by `ruff check --fix`.

**Sources**: [Makefile:16-18](), [CONTRIBUTING.md:43-49](), [.github/workflows/lint_production.yaml:34-37]()

### Clean Workspace

To remove all compiled Python files, `__pycache__` directories, and test/ruff caches:
```bash
make clean
```

**Sources**: [Makefile:8-13]()

## Model Development Workflow

### Adding a New Model

To incorporate a new model into the Foundry ecosystem:
1. Create a `models/<model_name>` directory.
2. Add a `pyproject.toml` specific to the model.
3. Define `foundry` as a dependency in the model's `pyproject.toml`.
4. Implement specific logic in `models/<model_name>/src/`.
5. Install in editable mode: `uv pip install -e ./models/<model_name>`.

**Sources**: [CONTRIBUTING.md:61-70]()

### Documentation Development

Foundry documentation is built using Sphinx with the Furo theme and MyST parser for Markdown support.

**Build Requirements**:
Install dependencies from `docs/docs_requirements.txt`:
```bash
uv pip install -r docs/docs_requirements.txt
```

**Building Locally**:
```bash
cd docs
make html
```

**Sources**: [CONTRIBUTING.md:72-84](), [docs/docs_requirements.txt:1-4](), [docs/source/conf.py:17-29]()

### Model Documentation Integration

Model-specific documentation is maintained within each model's directory and symlinked to the central documentation source.

1. Create `models/<model_name>/docs`.
2. Symlink to the main source:
   ```bash
   ln -s ../../../models/<model_name>/docs docs/source/models/<model_name>
   ```

**Sources**: [CONTRIBUTING.md:86-96]()

## Code Standards and Entity Mapping

The following diagram maps natural language development concepts to the specific code entities and files that implement them in the Foundry repository.

**Development Entity Map**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        Formatting["Code Formatting"]
        Training["Model Training"]
        Validation["Model Validation"]
        Dependency["Dependency Management"]
        DocBuild["Documentation Build"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Ruff["ruff (via Makefile)"]
        TrainScript["models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py"]
        ValScript["models/rf3/src/rf3/validate.py"]
        PyProject["pyproject.toml"]
        SphinxConf["docs/source/conf.py"]
    end

    Formatting --- Ruff
    Training --- TrainScript
    Validation --- ValScript
    Dependency --- PyProject
    DocBuild --- SphinxConf
```

**Sources**: [Makefile:16-18](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py:26](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/validate.py:25](), [docs/source/conf.py:9-12]()

## Testing and Validation

Tests for the core Foundry code are located in `foundry/tests`, while model-specific tests reside in their respective directories (e.g., `models/rf3/tests`).

**Test Configuration**:
Tests use fixtures and configuration utilities defined in `conftest.py` files.
- `configure_pytest`: Sets up the environment for model-specific tests.
- `get_test_data_dir`: Locates assets for unit testing.

**Sources**: [CONTRIBUTING.md:38-41](), [models/rf3/tests/conftest.py:3-10]()

This page provides guidelines for contributing code, documentation, and improvements to the Foundry repository. It covers code style conventions, development workflow, and the process for adding new models.

---

## Code Contributions

### Code Organization and Dependencies
The Foundry ecosystem follows a strict dependency hierarchy to ensure modularity and maintainability. All models within Foundry utilize [AtomWorks](https://github.com/RosettaCommons/atomworks) for structural manipulation.

- **AtomWorks**: Handles I/O, preprocessing structures, and data featurization [CONTRIBUTING.md:16-16]().
- **Foundry Core**: Contains shared model architectures, training infrastructure (`FabricTrainer`), and inference abstractions (`BaseInferenceEngine`) [CONTRIBUTING.md:17-17]().
- **Models**: Released models (e.g., `rfd3`, `rf3`) reside in the `models/` directory and use the structure provided by Foundry and AtomWorks [CONTRIBUTING.md:18-18]().

### Diagram: System Dependency Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "External Layer"
        AW["AtomWorks (External Repo)"]
    end

    subgraph "Foundry Core (foundry/src/foundry)"
        BIE["BaseInferenceEngine"]
        FT["FabricTrainer"]
        CR["CheckpointRegistry"]
    end

    subgraph "Model Layer (foundry/models/)"
        RFD3["RFD3 (rfd3/src/rfd3)"]
        RF3["RF3 (rf3/src/rf3)"]
        MPNN["MPNN (mpnn/src/mpnn)"]
    end

    AW --> BIE
    AW --> FT
    BIE --> RFD3
    BIE --> RF3
    BIE --> MPNN
    CR --> RFD3
```
**Sources:** [CONTRIBUTING.md:12-19]()

---

## Development Setup

### Installing in Editable Mode
For development, install both the core foundry package and all models in editable mode using `uv`. This allows immediate visibility of changes in shared utilities or specific models [CONTRIBUTING.md:20-29]().

```bash
uv pip install -e '.[all,dev]'
```

### Coding Standards
1.  **Variable Naming**: Use meaningful, descriptive names [CONTRIBUTING.md:33-33]().
2.  **Docstrings**: Use the **Google-format** for all docstrings to ensure compatibility with the Sphinx documentation builder [CONTRIBUTING.md:34-34]().
3.  **Style Guides**: Adhere to **PEP8** (Style) and **PEP20** (Zen of Python) [CONTRIBUTING.md:35-37]().
4.  **Formatting**: Foundry uses `ruff format` via pre-commit hooks. Enable them after cloning:
    ```bash
    pip install pre-commit
    pre-commit install
    ```
    This will automatically format your code during `git commit` [CONTRIBUTING.md:44-49]().

### Testing
Tests for the Foundry source code are located in `foundry/tests`, while model-specific tests reside in their respective directories (e.g., `models/<model>/tests`) [CONTRIBUTING.md:38-38](). 
*Note: Running tests is currently undergoing updates; some test files may be missing [CONTRIBUTING.md:39-41]().*

**Sources:** [CONTRIBUTING.md:20-41](), [CONTRIBUTING.md:44-49]()

---

## Pull Request Process

### Committing Changes
- **Logical Units**: Keep each commit focused on a single task or feature [CONTRIBUTING.md:52-52]().
- **Semantic Commits**: Adhere to [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) [CONTRIBUTING.md:53-53]().
- **Draft PRs**: Submit a draft PR early to solicit feedback from maintainers [CONTRIBUTING.md:54-54]().

### Finalizing the PR
- **Target**: Merge your branch into the `production` branch [CONTRIBUTING.md:57-57]().
- **Size Limit**: Keep PRs under **400 Lines of Code (LOC)** to ensure they can be reviewed within a reasonable timeframe (approx. 1 hour) [CONTRIBUTING.md:58-58]().

**Sources:** [CONTRIBUTING.md:51-58]()

---

## Adding a Model

To incorporate a new model as an independent package within the Foundry ecosystem, follow these steps:

1.  **Directory Structure**: Create `models/<model_name>` with a `pyproject.toml` [CONTRIBUTING.md:67-67]().
2.  **Dependencies**: Add `foundry` as a dependency in the model's `pyproject.toml` [CONTRIBUTING.md:68-68]().
3.  **Implementation**: Place model-specific logic in `models/<model_name>/src/` [CONTRIBUTING.md:69-69]().
4.  **Installation**: Users can then install the model via `uv pip install -e ./models/<model_name>` [CONTRIBUTING.md:70-70]().

### Diagram: Model Integration Logic

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "foundry/models/new_model/"
        TOML["pyproject.toml<br/>(depends on foundry)"]
        SRC["src/new_model/<br/>(Model Logic)"]
        DOCS["docs/<br/>(Markdown/RST)"]
    end

    subgraph "foundry/docs/source/models/"
        LINK["Symlink: new_model -> ../../../models/new_model/docs"]
    end

    SRC --> TOML
    DOCS -.-> LINK
```
**Sources:** [CONTRIBUTING.md:61-70](), [CONTRIBUTING.md:89-94]()

---

## Documentation Contributions

External documentation is built using **Sphinx** and hosted via **GitHub Pages** [CONTRIBUTING.md:73-73]().

### Building Documentation
Install documentation-specific dependencies and build the HTML:
```bash
uv pip install -r docs/docs_requirements.txt
cd docs
make html
```
**Sources:** [CONTRIBUTING.md:75-82](), [docs/docs_requirements.txt:1-4]()

### Documentation Organization
- **Foundry Core Docs**: Located in `docs/source/`. The `index.rst` acts as the landing page [CONTRIBUTING.md:87-87]().
- **Model Docs**: Each model maintains its own `docs/` folder. To make these visible to the main Sphinx build, a symlink must be created in `docs/source/models/` pointing to the model's internal documentation directory [CONTRIBUTING.md:89-94]().
- **Format**: Supports both **Markdown** (via `myst_parser`) and **ReStructured Text** [CONTRIBUTING.md:84-84](), [docs/source/conf.py:17-19]().

### CI/CD for Docs
Documentation is automatically built and deployed to the `gh-pages` branch upon pushing to the `production` branch via GitHub Actions [ .github/workflows/documentation.yml:22-30]().

**Sources:** [CONTRIBUTING.md:72-96](), [docs/source/conf.py:1-64](), [.github/workflows/documentation.yml:1-30]()

This glossary provides technical definitions for codebase-specific terms, domain jargon, and architectural concepts within the Foundry repository.

## Core Data Structures & Representations

### AtomArray
The primary data structure used for representing molecular systems, provided by the [AtomWorks](https://github.com/RosettaCommons/atomworks) library and based on `biotite.structure.AtomArray` [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:18-18](). It is a structure-oriented NumPy-like array where each row represents an atom and columns represent attributes (coordinates, chain ID, residue name, atom name, etc.).

### Atom14
A standardized representation of protein residues using a maximum of 14 heavy atoms. This fixed-size representation allows for efficient tensorized operations in neural networks like RFdiffusion3 and RosettaFold3 [models/rfd3/README.md:56-57]().

### Contig String
A mini-language used to specify the composition of a protein design target. It defines which parts of a structure are fixed (motif) and which are to be generated (diffused).
*   **Example**: `50-80,/0,A1-100` means: diffuse a monomer of length 50-80, followed by a chain break, then use residues 1-100 of chain A from the input structure as a fixed motif [models/rfd3/docs/input.md:39-39]().

### InputSelection
A mini-language used within the `InputSpecification` to select specific subsets of atoms or residues for conditioning (e.g., selecting ligands by name or specific residue ranges) [models/rfd3/docs/input.md:18-18]().

## Diffusion Terminology (RFD3)

### Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG)
A technique used during the reverse diffusion process to steer the model toward specific conditions (like hydrogen bond donors/acceptors) without requiring a separate classifier network [models/rfd3/docs/input.md:85-85](). It involves interpolating between a conditional and unconditional model prediction using a `cfg_scale` [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py:51-51]().

### Noise Schedule
A sequence of noise levels ($t$) defined from $T$ (pure noise) to $0$ (clean structure). RFD3 uses an EDM-style schedule [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py:66-75]().
*   **$p$**: Power constant determining the "shape" of the noise schedule (default: 7) [models/rfd3/docs/input.md:97-97]().
*   **$\gamma_0$**: A parameter influencing design diversity vs. designability [models/rfd3/docs/input.md:98-98]().

### Partial Diffusion
A mode where the process starts from a partially noised structure rather than pure Gaussian noise. This is used for "refining" or diversifying an existing structure [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py:89-93]().

### Recycling
An iterative process where the model's own outputs are fed back as inputs within a single denoising step to refine the structural prediction [models/rfd3/docs/input.md:83-83](). Controlled by `n_recycle` (default: 2) [models/rfd3/configs/inference_engine/rfdiffusion3.yaml:41-41]().

**Sources:** [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py:25-131](), [models/rfd3/docs/input.md:68-101](), [models/rfd3/configs/inference_engine/rfdiffusion3.yaml:24-51]()

## Model Architecture & Training

### Inference Engine
A high-level class abstraction (`BaseInferenceEngine`) that encapsulates the logic for loading checkpoints, preprocessing inputs, executing model forward passes, and saving outputs [src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py:22-22]().
*   **RFD3InferenceEngine**: Handles diffusion sampling and contig parsing [models/rfd3/configs/inference_engine/rfdiffusion3.yaml:6-6]().
*   **RF3InferenceEngine**: Handles structure prediction, MSA processing, and confidence scoring [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:222-222]().

### Tokenization
The process of grouping atoms into discrete units (tokens) for the transformer blocks. In Foundry, this often involves grouping atoms by residue [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/block_utils.py:33-54]().
*   **Low Memory Mode**: A memory-efficient tokenization strategy for handling large systems on limited GPU RAM [models/rfd3/docs/input.md:70-70]().

### Structure to Code Mapping

The following diagram maps high-level concepts to the specific classes and files implementing them.

**Conceptual Entity to Code Mapping**
```mermaid

        C["Diffusion Logic"]
        D["Input Spec"]
    end

    end

    A --- A1
    A1 --- A2

    style A1 stroke-dasharray: 5 5
    style B1 stroke-dasharray: 5 5
```
**Sources:** [src/foundry/inference_engines/base.py:22-22](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:222-222](), [src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py:80-122](), [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py:58-58]()

## RosettaFold3 (RF3) Confidence Metrics

RF3 outputs several metrics to validate the quality of predicted structures [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:99-110]():

| Metric | Definition | Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **pLDDT** | Predicted Local Distance Difference Test; measures per-residue confidence. | `get_mean_atomwise_plddt` [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:39-39]() |
| **pTM** | Predicted Template Modeling score; measures global topology confidence. | `ComputePTM` [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:51-51]() |
| **ipTM** | Interface pTM; measures confidence in the relative orientation of chains. | `ComputeIPTM` [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:52-52]() |
| **Ranking Score** | Weighted sum of ipTM and pTM used to select the best design. | `compute_ranking_score` [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:79-95]() |

## Infrastructure & Environment

### Checkpoint Registry
A centralized mapping of model names (e.g., `rfd3`, `rf3`, `proteinmpnn`) to their remote URLs, local filenames, and SHA256 hashes [src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py:80-122]().

### .env Configuration
A local file used to define paths to external tools and data mirrors [README.md:112-115]().
*   **PDB_MIRROR_PATH**: Path to a local mirror of the Protein Data Bank [env:13-13]().
*   **CCD_MIRROR_PATH**: Path to a local mirror of the Chemical Component Dictionary [env:22-22]().
*   **HBPLUS_PATH**: Path to the `hbplus` executable for hydrogen bond calculation [env:32-32]().

### Data Flow Diagram
This diagram illustrates how an input specification moves through the system components to produce a design.

**Foundry Data Pipeline**
```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["JSON/YAML Spec"] --> Engine["RFD3InferenceEngine"]
    Engine --> Sampler["SampleDiffusionWithMotif"]
    Sampler --> Model["RFD3_diffusion_module"]
    Model --> Output["RFD3Output (CIF + JSON)"]
    
    subgraph "Infrastructure"
        Registry["checkpoint_registry.py"] -.-> Engine
        Env[".env Paths"] -.-> Engine
    end
```
**Sources:** [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/run_inference.py](), [models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py:58-156](), [src/foundry/inference_engines/checkpoint_registry.py:80-122](), [models/rf3/src/rf3/inference_engines/rf3.py:99-110]()
